experiment_description: Use the SCOPE workflow—Solvation Characterization via Optimized Probability Ensemble averaging—to determine the local solvation microstate hierarchy for dilute aqueous LiCl at 298 K. The central idea being tested is that a finite-concentration electrolyte can be characterized by biasing one representative Li+ ion with metadynamics, reweighting the biased trajectory to recover equilibrium microstate probabilities, and applying a finite-water-reservoir chemical-potential correction based on water activity. Atomistic simulations are performed in LAMMPS with periodic boundary conditions using SPC/E water and AMBER Li+/Cl- ion parameters. Van der Waals interactions use a 10 Å real-space Lennard-Jones cutoff; short-range electrostatics use the same cutoff; long-range electrostatics use PPPM with convergence tolerance 1e-5. Each LiCl(aq) system is energy-minimized by conjugate gradient with force and energy tolerances of 1e-4 kcal/(mol Å) and 1e-4 kcal/mol, annealed by heating to 400 K for 10 ps and cooling back to 298 K in NVT with a Nose-Hoover thermostat relaxation time of 100 fs, equilibrated in NPT at 1 atm for 1 ns with a Nose-Hoover barostat relaxation time of 2 ps and a 1 fs timestep, resized to the equilibrium cell dimensions averaged over the final 250 ps, deformed to that size over 100 ps, equilibrated for another 500 ps in NVT, and then run for 5 ns in NVT at 298 K. For enhanced sampling, start each metadynamics walker from equilibrated classical-MD configurations and bias only one central Li+ ion. Use three collective variables: Li-O, Li-Cl, and Li-Li coordination numbers, each bounded from 0.0 to 7.0, with switching-function cutoff distances of 2.65 Å, 2.95 Å, and 5 Å, respectively. Store the free-energy surface on a grid with spacing 0.1. Add Gaussian hills every 1000 MD steps with hill weight 0.6 kcal/mol and hill width 1.25. Use 10 multiple-walker metadynamics walkers communicating every 25 ps. Extract Li+-centered clusters using Li-O and Li-Cl distance cutoffs of 2.65 Å and 3.05 Å, respectively; in the main coarse classification, solvent-separated ion-pair geometries are grouped into the solvated-ion category rather than treated as a separate microstate. Apply trajectory-space reweighting to recover unbiased microstate probabilities and compute relative Helmholtz free energies in units of kBT. Apply the finite-reservoir correction using water activity coefficients and define free water locally within a 12 Å sphere around the biased Li+ ion. Estimate statistical uncertainty by bootstrap resampling from starting frames 0 through 9 with a fixed 10-frame sampling interval. The spatial scope is the local solvation environment of the biased Li+ ion and the cluster identities generated from the first-shell Li-O/Li-Cl cutoffs, compared across the 10 walkers and bootstrap samples for the dilute 0.5 M condition.

dominant_microstate_0p5M_298K.description: The lowest-free-energy Li-centered solvation microstate identified by the SCOPE free-energy spectrum for dilute 0.5 M LiCl(aq) at 298 K.

second_microstate_0p5M_298K.description: The next-lowest-free-energy Li-centered solvation microstate identified by the SCOPE free-energy spectrum for dilute 0.5 M LiCl(aq) at 298 K.

dominant_solovation_family_0p5M_298K.description: The coarse solvation-family assignment of the lowest-free-energy local Li-centered microstate in dilute 0.5 M LiCl(aq) at 298 K.

experiment_description: Use the SCOPE workflow to compute the concentration-dependent corrected free-energy spectrum of LiCl(aq) at 298 K from dilute solution to beyond the solubility regime, testing the central proposed organizing principle that finite-concentration electrolytes evolve from hydration-dominated local states to ion-pair competition and then to aggregated Li-Cl clusters as ionic strength increases. Simulate LiCl(aq) concentrations spanning 0.5 M to 25 M at 298 K in LAMMPS with SPC/E water, AMBER Li+/Cl- parameters, periodic boundary conditions, 10 Å van der Waals and short-range electrostatic cutoffs, PPPM long-range electrostatics with 1e-5 convergence tolerance, and a 1 fs timestep. For each concentration, apply the same equilibration protocol: conjugate-gradient minimization to 1e-4 kcal/(mol Å) force tolerance and 1e-4 kcal/mol energy tolerance, NVT annealing through 400 K for 10 ps and back to 298 K using a Nose-Hoover thermostat with 100 fs relaxation time, 1 ns NPT equilibration at 1 atm using a Nose-Hoover barostat with 2 ps relaxation time, equilibrium cell averaging over the final 250 ps, deformation to the averaged cell over 100 ps, 500 ps additional NVT equilibration, and 5 ns NVT production. For SCOPE sampling, initialize multiple-walker metadynamics from equilibrated classical-MD snapshots; bias one central Li+ ion with Li-O, Li-Cl, and Li-Li coordination-number collective variables bounded between 0.0 and 7.0, using cutoffs of 2.65 Å, 2.95 Å, and 5 Å, respectively. Use a free-energy grid spacing of 0.1, add Gaussian hills every 1000 steps with 0.6 kcal/mol weight and 1.25 width, and use 10 walkers communicating every 25 ps. Identify local microstates by Li+-centered cluster extraction with Li-O = 2.65 Å and Li-Cl = 3.05 Å cutoffs. Reweight biased trajectories to obtain unbiased microstate probabilities and convert them to relative Helmholtz free energies in kBT. Apply the chemical-potential correction for finite water reservoir effects using water activity coefficients and the local free-water population inside a 12 Å sphere centered on the biased Li+ ion. The spatial/geometric scope is the biased-ion local environment and its connected Li-O/Li-Cl cluster within the periodic simulation cell, sampled across concentrations from 0.5 M through 25 M and compared through bootstrap resampling of trajectory frames.

predicted_solubility_limit_298K_M.description: The LiCl concentration at which the corrected SCOPE free-energy ordering indicates the aggregate family becomes the lowest-free-energy family at 298 K.

dominant_microstate_near_solubility_298K.description: The lowest-free-energy Li-Cl aggregate microstate identified near the 298 K solubility regime.

dominant_microstate_25M_298K.description: The lowest-free-energy larger aggregate microstate identified for LiCl(aq) beyond the 298 K solubility regime at 25 M.

aggregate_family_lowest_at_298K_solubili.description: Whether the aggregate family is the lowest-free-energy solvation family at the concentration assigned as the 298 K solubility regime by the corrected SCOPE analysis.

experiment_description: Use SCOPE to determine temperature-dependent solubility limits of LiCl(aq) by comparing corrected aggregate free energies with other Li-centered solvation families across temperature. The central concept is that the same enhanced-sampling, reweighting, and water-activity-corrected finite-reservoir framework can turn molecular dynamics trajectories into a predictive free-energy spectrum for concentrated electrolytes. Simulate LiCl(aq) in LAMMPS with SPC/E water and AMBER Li+/Cl- ion parameters under periodic boundary conditions at three temperatures: 283 K over 0.5 M to 23 M, 298 K over 0.5 M to 25 M, and 313 K over 0.5 M to 26 M. Use a 10 Å Lennard-Jones cutoff and 10 Å short-range electrostatic cutoff, PPPM electrostatics with convergence tolerance 1e-5, conjugate-gradient minimization to 1e-4 kcal/(mol Å) force tolerance and 1e-4 kcal/mol energy tolerance, NVT annealing through 400 K for 10 ps and back to the target temperature with a Nose-Hoover thermostat relaxation time of 100 fs, 1 ns NPT equilibration at 1 atm with a Nose-Hoover barostat relaxation time of 2 ps, 1 fs integration timestep, equilibrium-cell averaging over the final 250 ps, 100 ps deformation to the averaged cell, 500 ps NVT equilibration, and 5 ns NVT production. For enhanced sampling at each temperature and concentration, use 10-walker metadynamics initialized from equilibrated MD snapshots, biasing one central Li+ with Li-O, Li-Cl, and Li-Li coordination-number collective variables bounded from 0.0 to 7.0 with cutoff distances 2.65 Å, 2.95 Å, and 5 Å. Use grid spacing 0.1, Gaussian hills every 1000 steps, hill weight 0.6 kcal/mol, hill width 1.25, and walker communication every 25 ps. Extract Li-centered clusters using Li-O = 2.65 Å and Li-Cl = 3.05 Å cutoffs, reweight biased trajectories to unbiased probabilities, compute relative Helmholtz free energies in kBT, and correct for finite water reservoir effects using activity coefficients and free water counted within a 12 Å sphere about the biased Li+ ion. The spatial scope is the local first-shell and multi-ion cluster environment around one biased Li+ per periodic simulation box, compared over the full concentration sweeps and bootstrap-resampled trajectory frames at each temperature.

predicted_solubility_limit_283K_M.description: The LiCl concentration at which the corrected SCOPE free-energy ordering assigns aggregate microstates as the lowest-free-energy family at 283 K.

predicted_solubility_limit_298K_M.description: The LiCl concentration at which the corrected SCOPE free-energy ordering assigns aggregate microstates as the lowest-free-energy family at 298 K.

predicted_solubility_limit_313K_M.description: The LiCl concentration at which the corrected SCOPE free-energy ordering assigns aggregate microstates as the lowest-free-energy family at 313 K.

aggregate_family_lowest_at_each_temperat.description: Whether the aggregate family is the lowest-free-energy family at the SCOPE-assigned solubility concentration for each of the three simulated temperatures.

experiment_description: Evaluate the finite-reservoir chemical-potential correction within SCOPE for concentrated LiCl(aq), focusing on whether the local definition of free water and finite simulation-box size affect the concentration at which aggregates become the lowest-free-energy family. The central mechanism under test is that biased finite simulation boxes can distort cluster free energies when the free-water reservoir is limited, and that a water-activity-based correction restores bulk-relevant water chemical potential around the biased ion. Use the same LAMMPS/SPC-E/AMBER LiCl(aq) simulation and metadynamics protocol as the main SCOPE analysis: periodic cells; 10 Å van der Waals and short-range electrostatic cutoffs; PPPM electrostatics at 1e-5 tolerance; minimization to 1e-4 kcal/(mol Å) and 1e-4 kcal/mol; NVT annealing through 400 K for 10 ps; 1 ns NPT at 1 atm; 1 fs timestep; 100 ps deformation to the averaged cell; 500 ps NVT equilibration; 5 ns NVT production; 10-walker metadynamics on one Li+ ion using Li-O, Li-Cl, and Li-Li coordination-number collective variables from 0.0 to 7.0 with cutoffs 2.65 Å, 2.95 Å, and 5 Å; grid spacing 0.1; Gaussian hills every 1000 steps with 0.6 kcal/mol weight and 1.25 width; and walker communication every 25 ps. Identify microstates from Li-centered clusters using Li-O = 2.65 Å and Li-Cl = 3.05 Å cutoffs, reweight biased probabilities, and compute relative Helmholtz free energies. For the correction test, define free water for the chemical-potential term inside a sphere centered on the biased Li+ ion and vary the sphere radius from 10 Å to 14 Å around the nominal 12 Å choice. Separately compare finite-size behavior by repeating the corrected analysis for varied simulation-box dimensions. The spatial scope is the chemically local neighborhood around the biased Li+ ion, explicitly parameterized by the 10-14 Å free-water-counting sphere, and the comparison of cluster-stability trends across box dimensions.

crossover_concentration_changed_by_10_to.description: Whether varying the local free-water-counting radius over the tested range changes the aggregate-stability crossover concentration.

activity_correction_damps_box_size_bias.description: Whether applying the water-activity-based correction reduces simulation-box-size dependence in the computed aggregate cluster stability.

experiment_description: Perform a higher-resolution dilute-solution SCOPE classification test for 0.5 M LiCl(aq) to assess whether solvent-separated ion pairs are hidden inside the coarse solvated-ion category used in the main workflow. The central methodological issue is that the main SCOPE extraction is Li+-centered and groups non-contact Li+-Cl- configurations into a coarse solvated-ion family; this test adds Cl-centered connectivity to resolve solvent-separated and isolated solvated states while retaining the same enhanced-sampling and reweighting framework. Simulate 0.5 M LiCl(aq) with the same LAMMPS molecular dynamics protocol: SPC/E water, AMBER Li+/Cl- parameters, periodic boundary conditions, 10 Å Lennard-Jones and short-range electrostatic cutoffs, PPPM electrostatics with 1e-5 tolerance, conjugate-gradient minimization to 1e-4 kcal/(mol Å) and 1e-4 kcal/mol, annealing through 400 K for 10 ps, target-temperature equilibration at 298 K, NPT at 1 atm for 1 ns, 1 fs timestep, final-cell averaging over 250 ps, 100 ps deformation, 500 ps NVT equilibration, and 5 ns NVT production. Use the same single-Li+ 10-walker metadynamics settings: Li-O, Li-Cl, and Li-Li coordination-number collective variables bounded from 0.0 to 7.0 with cutoffs of 2.65 Å, 2.95 Å, and 5 Å; free-energy grid spacing 0.1; Gaussian hills every 1000 steps with 0.6 kcal/mol weight and 1.25 width; and walker communication every 25 ps. For the alternative extraction, include both Li+-centered and Cl--centered clusters and add a Cl-H distance cutoff of 2.85 Å. Divide the coarse solvated-ion family into solvent-separated ion pairs, defined as Li+ and Cl- separated by exactly one water molecule, and isolated solvated ions, defined as Li+ and Cl- separated by two or more water molecules. For composition-specific geometry analysis of LiCl[H2O]9, classify geometries with a simple Li+-Cl- distance cutoff of 3.2 Å to distinguish contact-ion-pair-like and solvent-separated-ion-pair-like motifs. The spatial scope is the local ion-water-ion connectivity network around Li+ and Cl- within the specified Li-O, Li-Cl, Cl-H, and Li-Cl-distance cutoffs, compared across bootstrap samples from the biased dilute-solution trajectory.

lowest_free_energy_class_0p5M_high_resol.description: The lowest-free-energy solvation class obtained when the dilute 0.5 M LiCl(aq) SCOPE extraction explicitly separates isolated solvated ions from solvent-separated ion pairs.

dominant_geometry_within_LiCl_H2O9.description: The more populated local geometry class within the fixed LiCl[H2O]9 composition under the high-resolution dilute-solution classification.

ssip_more_stable_than_cip_within_LiCl_H2.description: Whether the solvent-separated-ion-pair-like geometry has lower free energy than the contact-ion-pair-like geometry within the fixed LiCl[H2O]9 composition.
